steps.text: Whisk cream cheese, sour cream, and ranch dressing mix together in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in green onions, Cheddar cheese, and bacon bits. Cover and refrigerate overnight before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Potato Dip
raw_recipe.description: This baked potato dip is a creamy blend of classic baked potato toppings including sour cream, Cheddar cheese, green onions, and bacon.

video.description: Elevate your tailgate game with our step-by-step video tutorial on How to Make a Tailgate-Ready Loaded Baked Potato Dip. recipeInstructions.text: Whisk cream cheese, sour cream, and ranch dressing mix together in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in green onions, Cheddar cheese, and bacon bits. Cover and refrigerate overnight before serving.

review.reviewBody: I used my own homemade dry ranch dressing mix and upped the onions. I also splurged and used real bacon, a half pound that I cooked to a crisp and crumbled. The cheese I used was sharp cheddar. I threw this together early this morning and let it set most of the day until I got home from work, my husband and I have eaten most of it--there's nothing left for Christmas. Whoops. We loved it!

This is good! I tried to reduce fat and calories by using light sour cream, light cream cheese and 2% sharp cheddar; I didn't feel like the flavor of the dip was compromised. I used the entire container of sour cream instead of the 8oz called for in the recipe. The flavor of bacon was good, but not over-powering, using real bacon pieces (found by the salad dressing at the grocery store). I served Ritz reduced fat crackers along with veggies (red pepper, carrots and celery). A super easy recipe AND good?!? It's a keeper in my book :)PS- Even better after it sits overnight!
I didn't have ranch seasoning so I did half the amount of sour cream plus ranch dressing. Threw it all in a crock pot and served warm right away. Very good with tortilla chips.

Other than being super thick, this was fantastic. It was easy to put together once the prep from cooking and crumbling the bacon, shredding the cheese, and snipping the chives was done. The next time, I'd use a mixer to blend the cream cheese and sour cream with the ranch seasoning as the cream cheese tended to want to have tiny lumps that were a pain to whisk out. I took this to a potluck at work and it was a hit. I received many compliments on this "dip". I call it "dip" in quotations because it isn't dippable and is dense, so you really need a spoon to get a portion. I paired this with some thick cut french fry curls and it was just like eating a loaded baked potato with all the toppings, but much more fun. I could see this "dip" as being great with raw crunchy veggies, a spread for a tortilla and rolled up, on a cracker, or as a topping on a baked potato. I am adding this to my list of go-to party foods because this is a winner!

After reading some of the other reviews I made some changes. I doubled the recipe and added an extra brick of cream cheese and real bacon. I also added some fresh minced garlic and seasoned salt. I wasn't able to make it the night ahead, but did let it set in fridge about 30 min before serving. My guests loved it! Served it with baked potatoes, grilled steaks and grilled mushrooms/onions. It's great as a topping on the steak too; that's how I was eating leftovers!! Will definitely make again.

I made this exactly as written initially, it was too thick as a dip for a fragile potato chip so I added a bit more sour cream to make it more spreadable. I let it sit for over a day before serving it thinking it would give it great flavor.. It was just okay, maybe if you were to fry up real bacon it would taste a little better. I almost wonder if it would be better hot because of the cheeses in it. If I were to make it again I would probably add some fresh garlic and real bacon then I would try baking it in the oven for a half hour and see if that helps the consistency and flavor.

I thought this tasted good. I made 1/2 recipe with some leftover cream cheese and sour cream. That amount made about 1-1 1/2 cups. I used all the ingredients except I used low-fat dairy and for the bacon I used pre-cooked thick cut bacon. I microwaved the bacon and then crumbled it very fine. I tasted it with crackers and pretzels, but it honestly had the most baked potato flavor with potato chips. I wouldn't subtitute anything different other than them. This will work good for a pot-luck or party. It is like other cream cheese, sour cream, and seasoning dips but better with the bacon and cheese.

We make this dip all the time but we mix everything together except the cheddar cheese. Smooth mixture in a 8x8 baking dish, sprinkle the cheddar on top, & back at 350* till the cheese is melted & bubbly. Serve it warm with corn chips. Soooo yummy!

I liked this overall but it needed some adjustment. It was just too thick to be a good chip dip. It had good flavor but I agree that it was very salty. I think if you cut back on the cream cheese and on the ranch dip, this would be much better. As it was, it was used to top baked potatoes rather than as a chip dip because it was too thick to dip easily. As a baked potato topping, it was great.

absolutely delicious, but I added additional seasonings, tablespoon of garlic/basil Italian dressing, used actual bacon and garnished with 16 month aged cheddar and paprika... HUGE hit! I will actually put this ON baked potatoes from now on!

Very good! I used low fat cream cheese and my favorite low fat sour cream, Daisy brand, and it was still great. Not being a fan of salt, I used only ½ pack of ranch dressing. I also used Trader Joe’s nitrate free apple wood smoked bacon instead of canned bacon. Quick to throw together and perfect for an afternoon watching football, I will definitely make this again.

This spread, dip or whatever you'd like to call it is over the top salty. The flavor is ok, but the salt content from the ranch dressing destroyed the overall flavor. I tried to save it by adding milk to counteract the salt. I'd add other ingredients possibly more sourcream but I don't have any on hand to save this. IF I make it again, I'll try using half the packet of Ranch dressing and season it with my own spices. It seems as though this may be ok with raw vegetables as a dip. Definitely not with potato chips because it would be disastrous with the salt flavor.

I was looking for a thicker dip to put on top of a sliced cucumber and then top with a tomato as an appetizer. This worked out great. I didn't want it to be too salty but it was good to be a little salty with the veggies. I actually used French Onion Soup mix because I just love it. My friends thought it was terrific. I had cooked bacon so I used it. It was great.

Followed the recipe to a T and it was WAY too salty and too thick, like other comments said. 3-4/5 stars. Use half the cream cheese and half the ranch mix and it was perfect! Still thick but easier to scoop onto chips with a spoon.
Very tasty recipe! I left off the cream cheese and only used 1/2 packet of ranch dressing mix.
I made this and it's very good. It made too kuch for just me.
I was looking for a quick an easy recipe using sour cream as a main component of the dip. Omitted the bacon and ranch, added powdered onion & garlic.

I love this dip! The only change I made was omitting the green onion. It may be slightly on the salty side but the flavors are all there and it tastes awesome! We eat this with Fritos scoops and potato skin chips if we can find them. Definitely a go to dip to make:)
This become our extended family's go to dip for a few years now for gatherings. I double the sour cream, that is the only change I make.
Huge hit! I used 3-4 green onions, added tomatoes and an additional 4-6oz of sour cream to taste.
